close_reason: Added a crate-level 'Spec-driven divergences (deliberate, do not fix)' rustdoc section (item 1) defending the bare String at_type vs jscontact-types' Option<String>. Cites RFC 8984's zero-defaultType + 12+ mandatory-@type annotations and RFC 9553 §1.3.4's defaultType notion. References PLAN.md and bd:JMAP-sgrr.3. A future 'consistency' PR proposing Option<String> at_type now hits a rendered-rustdoc defense at the top of every cargo doc page.
description:
Every public struct in this crate has a bare 'pub at_type: String' field with #[serde(rename = "@type")] (e.g. src/lib.rs:123, 150, 234, 279, 318, 382, 405, 519, 544, 621, 658, 711). This diverges from the sibling jmap-jscontact-types where at_type is Option<String> with default + skip_serializing_if.

The divergence is correct and grounded in the specs:
- RFC 8984 has zero (verified by grep: 'defaultType' appears 0 times) defaultType annotations and 12+ '@type: "X" (mandatory)' annotations. JSCalendar requires @type on every sub-object.
- RFC 9553 §1.3.4 introduces defaultType and permits omitting @type in implied-type positions.

This is documented in PLAN.md §55-68, AGENTS.md design-constraints table, and bd:JMAP-sgrr.3.

What a future contributor might wrongly suggest: 'Make at_type Option<String> for consistency with jscontact-types'. The defense is: the workspace canonical-templates rule (workspace AGENTS.md) explicitly permits 'differences mandated by the relevant RFC or draft', and this is exactly that case. The spec-driven divergence is more important than visual symmetry across sibling crates.

If the consistency complaint persists, point them at the PLAN.md justification and the bead trail (bd:JMAP-sgrr.3).
title: Bare String at_type (vs Option<String> in jscontact) is spec-correct and well-defended — defend against 'consistency' PRs
